name: MonarchChartFrame
title: ChartFrame
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with slots; accessibilityChartDescriptor(_:) with AXChartDescriptor (Accessibility framework); Grid for the data table
summary: The card a chart sits in: title, description, header controls, legend, loading, empty and error states that keep the chart's height, and the data as a table through "View as table" and VoiceOver's chart descriptor.
whenToUse: Around any chart that Monarch does not draw itself, such as a Swift Charts Chart or a custom drawing, so it gets the same header, states and accessible data as every other chart.
whenNotToUse: For one headline number without a plot, use a card with text or MonarchDeltaIndicator. For a list of labelled values, use MonarchBarList or LabeledContent with the Monarch style.
api: init(_ title: String, description: String? = nil, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, table: MonarchChartTable? = nil, legend: [MonarchChartLegendItem] = [], hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, legendMarker: MonarchChartLegendMarker = .line, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, isTableToggleShown: Bool = true, keepsOneVisible: Bool = true, contentAccessibility: MonarchChartFrameContentAccessibility = .chart, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

enum MonarchChartFrameStatus { case ready, loading, empty, error }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name, shown as a heading.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title; also the summary of the chart descriptor.

options.name: table
options.description: The chart's data: categories by series. Enables "View as table" and the chart descriptor.

options.name: legend
options.description: Legend entries, shown with MonarchChartLegend while the chart is visible.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: Hidden series keys; given, the legend entries are toggles.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart: the source, the last update.

options.name: height
options.description: The height kept for the body in every status.

options.name: isTableToggleShown
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered when there is a table.

options.name: keepsOneVisible
options.description: Whether the legend keeps the last visible series from being hidden.

options.name: contentAccessibility
options.description: .contain keeps the chart's own elements (a legend with values, a selected bar) reachable; the chart gives its plot the descriptor itself.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls in the header, such as a period Picker.

states.name: ready
states.description: The chart, the legend and, after "View as table", the data table in its place.

states.name: loading
states.description: A muted placeholder of the chart's height, spoken as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "This chart didn't load." and Try again when onRetry is set; otherwise the message with a warning icon in the strong danger colour.

appearance: A MonarchCard (surface fill, subtle border, large corner radius). The title is subheading text in the default colour, the description and footer caption text in the muted colour. The loading placeholder uses the muted background fill. Table headers use the muted text colour with hairline dividers between rows. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ChartFrame is a figure that always renders the data table for screen readers and offers headingLevel, emptyActions and a controlled showTable. On iOS the data reaches VoiceOver as an AXChartDescriptor (Audio Graphs and the chart data rotor) instead of a hidden table; the table view state is internal; the empty state has no action slot; and the title is a heading without levels. Swift Charts charts already provide their own descriptor; giving the frame a table replaces it with the frame's. Android ships the same MonarchChartFrame.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.

With a table, the chart is one element labelled with the title and carries an AXChartDescriptor: a categorical x axis, a numeric y axis named by valueTitle, and one series per table column, with the app's formatted values as point labels.
In the table, the header row is one element with the header trait and each row is read as the category, then each series and its value; a gap is read as "No value".
The loading placeholder is read as "Loading chart" and has the updates-frequently trait.
The error without retry combines its icon and text into one element; with onRetry it is MonarchInlineErrorRetry.
Without a table, the chart content keeps its own accessibility.
edgeCases: A long title wraps and the actions move under the heading when they do not fit beside it.
A wide table scrolls sideways inside the card.
Gaps (nil values) are drawn as a dash, read as "No value" and left out of the chart descriptor.
The value axis always includes zero; a series with only zeros gets a range of 0 to 1.
Audio Graphs and the chart rotor were not tried with VoiceOver on a device; the descriptor itself is unit-tested.

examples.template:
MonarchChartFrame(
    {{title}},
    description: {{description}},
    table: MonarchChartTable(
        categoryTitle: {{dayTitle}},
        categories: [{{week.0.day}}, {{week.1.day}}, {{week.2.day}}, {{week.3.day}}, {{week.4.day}}],
        series: [MonarchChartTableSeries({{legend.label}}, values: [{{week.0.requests}}, {{week.1.requests}}, {{week.2.requests}}, {{week.3.requests}}, {{week.4.requests}}])]
    ),
    legend: [MonarchChartLegendItem({{legend.key}}, label: {{legend.label}}, color: .data1)],
    footer: {{footer}},
    height: {{height}}
) {
    Chart(Array([{{week.0.requests}}, {{week.1.requests}}, {{week.2.requests}}, {{week.3.requests}}, {{week.4.requests}}].enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, requests in
        AreaMark(x: .value("Day", index), y: .value("Requests", requests))
            .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.data1.opacity(0.18))
        LineMark(x: .value("Day", index), y: .value("Requests", requests))
            .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.data1)
    }
    .chartXAxis(.hidden)
    .chartYAxis(.hidden)
    .chartYScale(domain: .automatic(includesZero: false))
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
} actions: {
    MonarchSegmentedControl(
        "Range",
        selection: $range,
        items: [
            MonarchSegmentedItem({{ranges.0.label}}, value: {{ranges.0.value}}),
            MonarchSegmentedItem({{ranges.1.label}}, value: {{ranges.1.value}}),
        ],
        size: .sm,
        fillsWidth: false
    )
}
examples.setupTemplate:
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@State private var range = {{range}}
examples.setup:
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@State private var range = "7d"
examples.code:
MonarchChartFrame(
    "Requests",
    description: "New requests per day",
    table: MonarchChartTable(
        categoryTitle: "Day",
        categories: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"],
        series: [MonarchChartTableSeries("Requests", values: [48, 61, 55, 72, 66])]
    ),
    legend: [MonarchChartLegendItem("requests", label: "Requests", color: .data1)],
    footer: "Counts update every hour.",
    height: 96
) {
    Chart(Array([48, 61, 55, 72, 66].enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, requests in
        AreaMark(x: .value("Day", index), y: .value("Requests", requests))
            .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.data1.opacity(0.18))
        LineMark(x: .value("Day", index), y: .value("Requests", requests))
            .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.data1)
    }
    .chartXAxis(.hidden)
    .chartYAxis(.hidden)
    .chartYScale(domain: .automatic(includesZero: false))
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
} actions: {
    MonarchSegmentedControl(
        "Range",
        selection: $range,
        items: [
            MonarchSegmentedItem("7 days", value: "7d"),
            MonarchSegmentedItem("30 days", value: "30d"),
        ],
        size: .sm,
        fillsWidth: false
    )
}
